Subject: Finwave MAP: performance benchmarking plan + initial schedule

Hi Oliver / Sana —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, attached is a draft Mutual Action Plan that includes a focused performance evaluation we can run before you sign. High-level ask from Finwave: validate latency, throughput, TTFT and failover behavior across US / EU / APAC so you can finalize capacity planning.

Summary (see attached MAP-Finwave-draft.xlsx for details):
- Goals: confirm p95 latency targets and steady-state throughput for 2 model sizes; measure TTFT and cold-start penalty during region failovers.
- Success criteria (proposal): p95 <= 150ms (US), <= 200ms (EU), <= 250ms (APAC); TTFT median < 200ms for warmed sessions; sustain 250 req/s global (4k token avg) with concurrency 100.
- Test window: proposed 3-day window (2026-12-01 -> 2026-12-03).
- Deliverables: per-region latency CSV, failover log, consolidated load-test PDF, and updated MAP with go/no-go checklist.

We will need a staging API key and a short allowlist for test clients. Can you confirm procurement timeline (your team mentioned mid-December) so we can align the final sign-off?

Next step: confirm the 3-day window and any blackout windows for your environment. I cc'ed Laura and Marcus from Solutions/Perf so they can take ownership of the test plan.

Attachments: MAP-Finwave-draft.xlsx

Thanks,

Subject: Re: FW: Finwave MAP: performance benchmarking plan + initial schedule

Team / Oliver —

Proposed benchmarking plan (summary):
- Model: redwood-1.1-quant (int8-like profile we validated in staging).
- Test types: steady-state sustained throughput, burst/spike, concurrency ramp, and controlled region outage + recovery.
- Token profile: avg 800 tokens per request (conversation-style), 95th percentile 2,500 tokens for stress runs.
- Client locations: us-west (Ashburn -> internal agent), eu-west (Frankfurt), apac-sin (Singapore).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, TTFT (first token after request), throughput (req/s), CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit ratio, failover detection time and cold-start penalty.
- Batching / runtime flags: continuous batching enabled; batch size target 8-16 depending on sequence length; KV cache warmup runs before steady-state.

Failover test plan:
1) Establish steady-state global load for 60m.
2) Kill region route (simulate outage) for EU for 5m; observe detection and routing to fallback region + any cold-starts.
3) Re-instate route and measure warmup.

Pre-test: 2 warmup runs (per region) and baseline 30m of steady-state to stabilize caches. Post-test: consolidation and 2h for logs and profiling.

Schedule: propose run 2026-12-01 -> 2026-12-03 (3 days). Day 1: baseline + steady-state; Day 2: failover experiments; Day 3: spikes and re-runs after config tweaks.

I'll attach the raw load profiles (regional-load-profiles.json) and a short runbook. Priyom can run the harness; Rishi please confirm routing policy (health check intervals, fallback order).

Marcus Lin
Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finwave.ai>, Sana Iqbal <sana.iqbal@finwave.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2026 09:01:00 -0800
Subject: Finwave perf tests — Day 1 results (summary)

Oliver / team —

We completed Day 1 (baseline + steady-state) and ran the first failover sequence as a sanity check. Attachments: regional-latency-results.csv, load-test-report.pdf (high level).

High-level numbers (median / p95 / p99):
- US (us-west): p50 78ms / p95 118ms / p99 240ms; TTFT median 140ms. Sustained throughput: 270 req/s with 100 concurrency at avg 800 tokens.
- EU (eu-west): p50 110ms / p95 175ms / p99 360ms; TTFT median 210ms.
- APAC (apac-sin): p50 155ms / p95 220ms / p99 520ms; TTFT median 260ms.

Failover sanity check (simulated EU outage):
- Detection + route switch observed: ~320ms (median across orchestrator logs).
- Cold-start penalty for new regional worker spun up from idle: observed +480-550ms extra on first few requests; subsequent requests drop back toward baseline after KV cache warms (approx 3-5 minutes).

Observations & recommendations:
- Baseline meets proposed US p95 target; EU and APAC p95 are within expected geo delta but EU p99 and APAC p99 need attention for SLAs.
- Failover RTO (route switch) is under 400ms, but cold-start penalty increases TTFT on first requests in a new region. Options: pre-warm standby capacity, reduce health-check window, or implement fast-failover to a warmed fallback model.
- Suggested config tweaks: increase KV cache replication TTL, lower health check window to 1s for critical routes, set warm standby for APAC if tight SLA required.

We can iterate Day 2 with the above changes (shorter health-checks + one warmed standby per region) and re-run the failover sequence. Confirm if Finwave wants the warmed standby enabled for Day 2.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Perf Engineer, Redwood Inference
